rv.q: Impish and brimming with originality, this is fringe theatre at its most scintillating and inventive.
It’s the scrappy upstart to The Book of Mormon’s slick West End production; a winning combination of nerdy musical theatre and boundary-pushing obscenities.
Enthusiastically performed, the show couldn’t quite sustain its high-octane energy to the end, such that proceedings started to flag, even as the storyline became ever more absurd.
This is a show unlike anything I have ever seen before, and I found myself as enraptured as any show I have ever seen about the rapture.

cn.t: Critics praise this audaciously original musical comedy about religious manipulation and butt plugs as inventive, scintillating fringe theatre that's surprisingly touching beneath its brazen premise.
